reuse.why: The change extends the existing recurrence and weekend helpers and shares holiday matching, although consumers still assemble occurrence processing separately.

duplication.why: Daily exclusion followed by conditional date adjustment is repeated across getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, and getDatesInRange.

placement.why: Holiday primitives belong in shared/schedules.ts, but the server handlers also retain scheduling policy that would fit better alongside those primitives.

scope.why: The implementation, tests, model extension, and release note all address the requested scheduling changes.

maintainability.why: Maintainers must coordinate recurrence filtering, holiday exclusion, fetch sizing, date adjustment, and a separate fixed range-padding assumption across multiple functions.

bypasses_abstraction.where: The changed consumers use recurConfigToRSchedule and getDateWithSkippedWeekend rather than implementing independent recurrence or holiday adjustment algorithms.

disguised_duplication.where: The exclusion-and-adjustment pipeline appears as an isOccurrence predicate plus imperative adjustment in getNextDate and as filter/map chains with different adjustment gates in the two server handlers.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend gains the holidays parameter, and recurConfigToRSchedule gains a daily skipWeekend branch; consumers continue using these helpers, but occurrence-processing orchestration remains distributed.
